_note: Your job hunt settings. The skill reads this every run. Setup ('set up job hunt') writes it; edit it any time. Search terms, sources, auto-drop rules and locations live in the Google Sheet instead.
name: Full Name
_levelOptions: graduate | junior | mid | senior | any. Sets which default Auto-drop rules and sources are switched on.
experience: One line on your experience, e.g. '3 years as a registered nurse' or 'final-year accounting student'.

targets.summary: One line: what you're looking for, in priority order.

groups.label: Main
groups.roles: The roles you want most, e.g. registered nurse, junior accountant, marketing coordinator, software engineer
groups.resumeAngle: How the resume summary should be pitched for these roles

groups.label: Also
groups.resumeAngle: How to pitch the summary for these instead

greenFlags: Things that make a role a good fit
redFlags: Things that make a role a poor fit

availability.emailRule: Never state a start date or notice period in contact emails.

contactEmailOptions._note: namedContacts: also find named HR or recruiting people with a published email. genericInbox: also include the company's published jobs, HR or general inbox.

resumeOptimisation._note: rewriteExperience: allow rewording experience lines to match the ad (only using facts already in resume.json). keywordTarget: share of the ad's key terms the resume should cover before it's flagged.

coverLetter.intro: Here is what caught my eye about your job posting and how I think my experience can benefit your team:
coverLetter.close: Thank you for considering my application and I look forward to hearing from you soon.

writingRules: No apologising for gaps or underselling yourself
Name real gaps plainly and say how they'd be closed
